title: Mark, Don't Erase: Token Inoculation for Dual-Use Knowledge in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2607.18639v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In a dual-use field, hazardous knowledge and the benign expertise around it share vocabulary, concepts, and causal structure. That overlap makes selective refusal hard, and existing methods such as unlearning and refusal training overgeneralize their suppression into the benign side. We argue for conditioning, not suppression. In this work, we introduce Token Inoculation, which marks hazardous sentences with a special token, the inoculation token, during continued pre-training. We then fine-tune the model to refuse hazardous questions and, on the same questions under the inoculation token, to predict the hazardous answers. At test time the inoculation token is absent, so the model does not express the hazardous answers it learned to predict. translated_title: 标记而非抹除：面向大语言模型两用知识的Token接种方法
translated_abstract: 在两用领域中，危险知识与围绕它的良性专业知识共享词汇、概念和因果结构。这种重叠使得选择性拒绝变得困难，而诸如去学习和拒绝训练等现有方法会将其抑制过度泛化到良性知识一侧。我们主张采用条件化而非抑制。在本工作中，我们提出了Token接种方法，在继续预训练期间用一个特殊标记（即接种标记）来标记危险句子。随后我们微调模型，使其拒绝危险问题，同时在带有接种标记的相同问题上预测危险答案。在测试时，接种标记并不存在，因此模型不会表达它学会预测的危险答案。在1.5B到14B参数范围以及三种架构家族中，该方法将危险准确率保持在约18%，同时保留了指令基线93%的MMLU性能，实现了最佳的安全-效用平衡。
tldr: 提出“Token接种”方法，在继续预训练时用特殊标记标注危险句子并训练模型条件化地预测危险答案，测试时因标记缺失而抑制危险输出，从而在保持93%良性性能的同时将危险准确率控制在约18%。
en_tdlr: Proposes "Token Inoculation," which marks hazardous sentences with a special token during continued pre-training and trains the model to condition its predictions on the token, so that at test time the absent token suppresses hazardous answers, keeping hazardous accuracy near 18% while retaining 93% of benign utility.
